architectureDecisions: Select a thin Node runtimeAdapter over a Python OpenHands SDK driver. DomainExecutionController continues to create and pin the semantic execution attempt; the adapter maps its runtimeInvocationKey to exactly one durable OpenHands conversation.

Pin OpenHands software-agent-sdk 1.49.4 and openhands-tools from monorepo commit 3f47426e6af4681aacab735c781426aae58a3bac. Its LocalConversation create-or-resume path persists base state and events, supports a fixed conversation_id, and can resume with agent=None in a fresh process.

Use the BB-065 request-tracker workspace prepared by the caller. The adapter accepts a canonical workspace root, immutable starting tree/hash, task ID, prompt ref/hash and output directory; it does not clone repositories, select work, or publish source.

Store an immutable attempt manifest before launching Python under <output>/attempts/<sha256(runtimeInvocationKey)>/manifest.json. It pins executionAttemptId, runtimeInvocationKey hash, workspace root and starting tree, strategy/toolset/model/harness refs, SDK commit/version, profile hash, conversation UUID and persistence directory.

Dispatch uses exclusive manifest creation. If a manifest already exists it returns UNKNOWN with recoveryRequired=true and performs no provider call. Recover validates the exact manifest and workspace identity, then reopens the same conversation ID/persistence directory; mismatch returns BLOCKED and never creates another conversation.

OpenHands owns conversation events and tool execution state inside the adapter. ExHarness owns attempt lifecycle, policy pins, runtime attestation, completion evaluation and publication authority. OpenHands completion maps only to a runtime result candidate.

Timeout sends SIGTERM to the driver, waits a bounded grace period, then SIGKILL if required and returns UNKNOWN/recoveryRequired. Cancellation uses AbortSignal with the same sequence. Process exit, signal, stdout/stderr digests and recovery decision are captured without secrets.

Use only TerminalTool and FileEditorTool in the selected profile. The driver rejects additional tool names, workspace escape, mutable branch/ref dependencies, and a model/profile different from the immutable manifest.

Reject Restate at eda4cf97ec8794614329d97078a3c8c3a8701c4f because a new BSL server duplicates delivered attempt recovery authority; reject Temporal server at 543367eec690da3c23e536cf5dfe76928af11b2c and LangGraph at 1211af45b18cab9c0a7efe366ba12f51ad2a9996 because their workflow/checkpoint authorities add a second lifecycle for this single domain-local adapter.

Reject mini-SWE-agent at 04d809ceab9df28f9adaed044884180159172930 as the integrated strategy: it is the direct baseline selected by BB-065 and intentionally runs independent subprocess actions, while its documented saved history is not a durable fresh-process conversation resume contract. Reject SWE-agent at 3ea751c087f32b16e039a2233dd6eefecef325d5 because trajectory replay is inspection/re-execution rather than continuation of the same live attempt.
implementationSlices: S1 — Add the strict Node adapter contract, immutable attempt-manifest codec, runtime result mapping and export; test collision, identity mismatch, policy drift, timeout, cancellation, secret redaction and the no-second-session invariant with a fake driver.

S2 — Add the pinned Python 3.12 OpenHands driver and uv lock. Construct only the allowed tools, create a new conversation on dispatch, resume with agent=None on recover, persist events under the exact conversation ID and emit one bounded JSON result.

S3 — Connect the delivered BB-065 fixture/profile to the live probe after the dependency is DONE. Run dispatch, deliberately interrupt after a persisted tool event, start a fresh Node/Python process, call recover and independently assess the workspace through BB-065 acceptance.
S4 — Record exact source/SDK/model/config/process/evidence identities, document the supported strategy and limitations in Living Docs, then submit the exact candidate and evidence to Jev.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A credential-bearing live probe routes one released DomainExecutionController claim through runtimeAdapter.dispatch into OpenHands SDK 1.49.4 at the pinned commit, edits the delivered BB-065 fixture, and produces bounded raw runtime evidence plus independent BB-065 acceptance evidence.
evidenceRequired: Exact candidate/tree, work and executionAttempt IDs, runtimeInvocationKey hash, SDK commit/version, model/profile/toolset hashes, starting and resulting workspace tree hashes, process result, redacted stdout/stderr digests and independent fixture acceptance report.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: After deliberate interruption following durable OpenHands activity, a fresh Node and Python process recovers the same executionAttemptId, conversation UUID, persistence directory and workspace; no second provider session or semantic attempt is created.
evidenceRequired: Pre-interruption durable event marker, process identities, manifest hash, identical conversation/attempt IDs before and after recovery, event sequence continuation and a session-creation count of exactly one.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Missing/corrupt persistence, starting-tree drift, profile/tool/strategy mismatch and an ambiguous killed process return BLOCKED or UNKNOWN with recoveryRequired and perform no fresh dispatch.
evidenceRequired: Deterministic negative-case logs and assertions proving provider spawn count does not increase.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Timeout and AbortSignal cancellation terminate the child through bounded TERM/KILL handling, retain process/evidence metadata and never map an ambiguous external effect to SUCCEEDED.
evidenceRequired: TERM/KILL trace, exit/signal data, bounded elapsed time and UNKNOWN result assertions.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: OpenHands status and driver output cannot publish, accept, mutate Blackboard/Oracle authority, change the pinned ExecutionAttemptBinding or bypass completionEvaluator/publicationGate.
evidenceRequired: Boundary tests with forged success/publication fields plus passing existing domain execution control regression.

evidenceRequired: uv lock audit output, resolved commit/version and startup mismatch rejection.

negativeVerificationCases: A second dispatch for an existing runtimeInvocationKey must not spawn Python or call a provider.
Recover with missing/corrupt OpenHands base state or a different conversation ID must fail closed.
Workspace starting tree, SDK commit, model profile, toolset, harness or strategy drift must not resume.
SIGTERM timeout or cancellation with no conclusive driver result must produce UNKNOWN, never SUCCEEDED.
A driver payload containing acceptance, publication or Blackboard mutation fields must be rejected.
Secrets present in environment or provider exceptions must not appear in manifest, stdout/stderr evidence or result JSON.
Agent-declared success with failing BB-065 independent acceptance must remain a rejected completion candidate.

recoveryProtocol.timeoutCancellation: Send SIGTERM, wait at most 5 seconds, then SIGKILL. Record signals and return UNKNOWN unless the driver had atomically published a complete result.
recoveryProtocol.missingEvidence: BLOCKED for identity/config/persistence mismatch; UNKNOWN for potentially executed but unresolved external effect.
